profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Software developer specializing in the development of mobile and embedded applications.

Specialties: Mobile, Embedded, J2ME, JME, Java, Smalltalk

positions.title: Chief Technology Officer/Founder
positions.description:
• Established company from concept, business plan, funding, sales, strategy, all the way to 42 employees
• Created business plan and prototypes for wireless sensor nodes based systems to track assets, Internet of Things (IoT)
• Created a mobile refurbishing and reverse logistics consulting business, which turned into main product line of company
• Created initial prototypes, led architecture, development practices, created sales and marketing collateral, performed sales pitches, negotiated contracts, performed customer support, product owner
• Achieved millions in revenue, millions in rounds of financing, signed a number of Tier 1 reverse logistics providers in the world

positions.title: Principal Investigator
positions.description:
• The work on Project Squawk (http://research.sun.com/projects/squawk/) entailed taking a Java VM written in Java, getting it Java certified and continuing research on how to integrate Java into the micro embedded space.  The Squawk VM is currently in production on the Sun SPOT wireless sensor device ( http://www.sunspotworld.com).  Squawk is now being used to target Java to the micro embedded space.  The intent is to have Java running on resource constrained CPUs, as well as down to small MCU microcontrollers.  Squawk is being designed to be completely written in Java and provide the smallest and most efficient execution engine for Java on resource constrained devices.
• Technical lead on bringing Java as programming language to FIRST Robotic Competition
• JavaOne 2008-2010 Program Committee Chair
• JavaOne 2009 Rockstar Award, JavaOne 2009 Duke's Choice Award
• Responsible for the introduction of the Java programming language to the FIRST Robotics Competition

positions.title: Staff Engineer
positions.description:
• Java Studio Creator, a visual development environment for web applications using Java and JSF, built on Netbeans
• I was responsible for InSync, the module responsible for the source modeling capabilities of the tool.  Creator provides a developer with the ability to drag and drop components, edit various properties of components, as well as edit raw source.  InSync was responsible for taking all graphical and component modifications and turn them into source code, as well as taking the source code and creating an object model from which the tool would use to support graphical and manual manipulations of the application.  The mantra of Creator was to have "truth in source", which meant all graphical manipulation of an application should be made persistent via source code, without any extra meta-data.  The reverse was also to be true, source should be used to re-create the graphical representation of the application.  InSync was the module responsible for achieving this.

positions.title: Director
positions.description:
• Volunteered as a mentor and teacher to middle and high school kids in the power of programming
• Helped manage the monthly operations of the school
• Created a new robotic competition called IAROC, to give the kids a robotic competition focused mainly on the software side of robotics
• Had to create multiple creative ways to keep kids engaged, example.  One child was very artistic and was not seeing the point of how one could be creative with programming.  I created a set of lessons for him where we started with creating stop motion movies using modeling clay.  This enabled the child to learn how to model things in the real world.  Then we switched to building the same models but using CAD software, enabling the child to model using algorithms rather than physical manipulation.  We were then able to go into Java 3D, of which not too many people were comfortable with in those days.

positions.title: Lead Architect
positions.description:
• Brought multiple consumer oriented mobile products from concept to market: included prototyping, design, architecture, implementation, testing/QA, maintenance, deployment to various carrier vending systems. Products included NASCAR.com To Go, Catholic Exchange, Youbet Anywhere, Caliente Betting.
• Responsible for development of a markup rendering and execution based client, along with authentication, content delivery and content generation server.
• Developed a unique synchronization technique that allowed a client to be updated in a single HTTP request, without having server store or perform complex dynamic computations.
• Managed and maintained data center to support development, testing and production servers supporting our various products.
• Gained extensive experience on the many differences, debugging techniques, and bugs to be found on a large number of devices supporting J2ME and BREW.

positions.title: Technical Lead
positions.description:
• Defined corporate strategy on development strategies for sometimes and always connected mobile solutions.
• Developed tools and mobile platform to enable enterprise developers to create enterprise ready mobile solutions. Mobile platform consisted of a base open source runtime environment with custom enhancements to support enterprise level requirements, as well as a complete framework.
• Jointly architected server based synchronization services. Services included optimized sending and receiving of data, using XML, as well as server based logic to connect to application servers. Researched syncML.
• Led development of mobile applications to support Peregrine’s suite of infrastructure management products: workorder management, receiving, asset tracking (IMAC), inventory management and more.
• Managed the delivery of key releases of mobile products, from inception to GA release.
• Provided education, both internally and externally, on key concepts and issues of mobile and wireless applications, such as the differences in WAN and WLAN issues, batch vs real-time solutions.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Worked on all aspects of architecting and building a unique platform for Internet Appliances.  This platform was to provide hardware OEMs and Service providers with software and services for the devices and services they were selling.  The platform included a unique and entirely new paradigm and user experience for resource limited internet oriented services.  Provide complete re-branding of the capabilities of the platform to fit any OEM/Service Provider requirements.  The client and server were in Squeak Smalltalk and Linux.
• Worked to integrate prior Pocket Java work into the client platform to allow customizations by clients to be made using Java, providing known technologies to OEM & Service Providers to work with.
• Architected and developed fault tolerant persistence for user documents on the device.  Included support for failure to read directory or file entries, issue of writing to solid state memory, use of journaling (ReiserFS)
• Architected printing services to attach to open ghost and other open source printing services.

positions.title: Director
positions.description:
• Jointly developed Pocket Smalltalk IDE and virtual machine.  Virtual machine is 24K in size and supports a full Smalltalk runtime on Palm Powered™ devices.  IDE is written in Smalltalk, including visual tools and full compiler.  Public site www.pocketsmalltalk.com.
• Created Pocket Java which supports Java 1.1.8 and is a hybrid Java and Smalltalk runtime and virtual machine.  Extended Pocket Smalltalk tools and VM with a full Java class file reader, Java simulator, Java decompiler, Java bytecode translator to extended Pocket Smalltalk bytecodes and optimizing cross-compiler.
• Made multiple public presentations to show Pocket Java and Pocket Smalltalk technology at various trade shows, including OOPSLA, Smalltalk Solutions and various Smalltalk and Java user groups.
• Director of a small business that developed various products for Palm Powered™ devices as well as providing expert consulting services to various clients.  See below for more details on consulting engagements.

positions.title: Lead Architect, Mentor
positions.description:
• Responsible for providing assistance with the customization, roll out and deployment of the Re-Insurance system built by CSC (See prior employement).
• Design and development of XML-driven computer interchange of data, loosely similar to EDI transactions.
• Led analysis of performance of persistence mechanism across a WAN, by analyzing introduction of the Gemstone OODBMS, prototyping a 3-tier architecture using Oracle PL/SQL stored procedure.
• Education and mentoring of employees to increase their own capabilities as system architects.
• Coordination of development of additional architectural and application functionality, with teams distributed throughout the US, UK and Germany, including design and code reviews.

positions.title: Lead Architect, Mentor
positions.description:
• Designed, implementated and maintained a series of frameworks and tools to ease the development of a Re-Insurance system by novice Smalltalk developers. 
• Design and development of a custom framework to provide isolation between domain objects, business logic and presentation.  This framework was deemed to be solid and mature enough to be sold as its own product.
• Participation in all levels of decision making regarding all technologies and architectural components to be used by system: Object-Oriented Database, Relational Database, development environment, 2 and 3 tier architectures, frameworks to support security, GUI presentation layer.
• Development of infrastructure to support incoming and outgoing EDI transactions.
• Mentor to a team of 18 developers whose previous Smalltalk experience was limited to a 2 week training course, provided a technical university approach to learning: including classes and code/peer reviews.

projects.title: Squawk JVM
projects.description: Squawk is an open-source Java virtual machine (JVM), written itself in Java. It's designed for running on small embedded devices (smaller than cell phones), such as wireless sensor devices, smart grid devices, robotics, etc. Squawk is the basis for the Sun SPOT software (http://www.sunspotworld.com) as well as the Java used in the FIRST Robotics Competition.

patents.title: Systems and methods for modifying content of mobile communication devices
SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR TESTING CONTENT OF MOBILE COMMUNICATION DEVICES
